briefTitle: Improving Primary Care Access to Urinary Incontinence Treatment for Women Veterans
officialTitle: Improving Primary Care Understanding of Resources and Screening for Urinary Incontinence to Enhance Treatment

arms.label: Women Veterans receiving primary care in VISN-7 of the VA Healthcare Administration (VHA)
arms.description: This project will include English-speaking, community-dwelling women Veterans 20 years or older with a diagnosis of UI (all types) and access to the internet via a mobile device or computer. Women Veterans who are currently pregnant or less than 12 weeks postpartum will be excluded. PURSUIT utilizes a mobile health application, called MyHealtheBladder, to connect patients with nonsurgical treatment options.
interventions: Behavioral: Mobile Health Application focused on behavioral treatments to treat urinary incontinence

arms.label: Health care providers in community-based outpatient clinics in VISN-7 of the the VHA
arms.description: Community-Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs) from VA Integrated Service Network (VISN) 7 will be targeted, spanning the states of Alabama, Georgia, and South Carolina. VISN 7 CBOCs, serving at least 50 women Veterans with primary care services, will be recruited.

interventions.name: Mobile Health Application focused on behavioral treatments to treat urinary incontinence

eligibility.text:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Veteran
* English-speaking, community-dwelling women Veterans
* Diagnosis of UI (all types)
* Access to the internet via a mobile device or computer

Exclusion Criteria:

* Women Veterans who are currently pregnant or less than 12 weeks postpartum
